newsitem.title: USA: N.J. family stable after small plane crash ordeal.
newsitem.headline: N.J. family stable after small plane crash ordeal.

text.p: A Milford, N.J., family was recovering on Monday after having spent about 17 hours in the wreckage of their small plane over Thanksgiving weekend, officials said.

Gary and Marie Knapp and their two young daughters were taken to Pocono Medical Centre after rescuers found them Sunday in the fuselage of their small plane, which had crashed in woods and heavy underbrush the night before.
Medical centre spokeswoman Janet Scheel said the condition of all four was "stable" but declined to give details.

The family was returning Saturday evening from a holiday trip to Massachusetts when pilot Gary Knapp radioed a distress call to air-traffic controllers, indicating a "fuel problem," said Harry Robidoux, director of emergency services for Monroe County, Pa.

The plane then disappeared from radar and its emergency beacon was activated. Search crews called out to look for the plane were hampered by poor weather that forced them indoors for a couple of hours before dawn Sunday, Robidoux said.
"It was raining constantly, heavy fog ... it was so bad, so foggy, they (rescuers) couldn't see their hands in front of their faces," he said.
The Knapps were found at about 10:30 a.m. EST Sunday, 17 hours after the distress call, in their plane on a wooded plateau in Tunkhannock Township, Pa., about 80 miles north of Philadelphia.

"They were in relatively good condition ... they were tired, cold, slightly wet," Robidoux said. He said Marie Knapp had a possible broken arm and one of the daughters may have suffered a slight skull fracture.
The cause of the crash was under investigation by federal authorities, he said.
